label: Credits reached end
summary: Whether the credits roll has reached its end.
details: Going by its name and its one use, the credits window uses it to show or hide an element: vanilla hides it with Not( ) once the end is reached.

label: Credits at fastest
summary: Whether the credits already scroll at their fastest speed.
details: Vanilla hides the Faster button of the credits screen while this is true.

label: Credits paused
summary: Whether the credits are paused.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the text of the pause button: the 'continue' text while paused, the 'pause' text otherwise.

label: Credits at slowest
summary: Whether the credits already scroll at their slowest speed.
details: Vanilla hides the Slower button of the credits screen while this is true.

label: Close credits
summary: Closes the credits screen.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Close button in the top right corner of the credits. It returns nothing.

label: Credits faster
summary: Makes the credits scroll faster.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Faster button of the credits screen, which is hidden once the fastest speed is reached. It returns nothing.

label: Credits slower
summary: An action of the credits window, going by its name to slow the credits down.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla names it as the on_start hook of a credits window element, so it runs when that element starts. What it does to the credits speed is not shown.

label: Toggle credits pause
summary: Going by its name, switches the credits between paused and running.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click and in an on_finish hook of the credits window. Going by its name it flips between paused and running; the input does not show more.

label: Credits window
summary: The credits window itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. The name Self is used on many types; the example lines in the input belong to other types and only hint at this use.

label: Culture (access)
summary: The culture itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Going by its name only; the example lines in the input belong to other types and only hint at the use.

label: Can add tradition
summary: Whether the culture can add a new tradition.
details: Vanilla uses it once, as Not( ... ) in the visible condition of an element of the culture window, so that element shows when it is false. What the element is is not shown; the meaning rests on the name.

label: Can diverge
summary: Whether the culture can diverge into a new culture.
details: Going by its name. The culture window uses the same name on the player's culture inside Not( ), so an element shows when it is false. That line may belong to another type, so this is a hint.

label: Can hybridize with
summary: Whether the culture can form a hybrid culture with another culture.
details: Going by its name. The culture window calls it on the player's culture with the viewed culture, inside Not( ), so an element shows when it is false.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture to hybridize with.

label: Culture custom text
summary: A named piece of text for the culture, from the game's custom localization.
details: It returns text. Going by its name only: the name appears on other types in vanilla (for example Character.Custom with a name in quotes), which suggests the argument is the name of a custom localization entry. No vanilla line uses it on a culture.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Cultural acceptance
summary: The cultural acceptance between the culture and another culture, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage, with the player's own culture passed in. Which way round the acceptance runs (who accepts whom) is not shown by the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture the acceptance is about.

label: Acceptance baseline text
summary: Text for the baseline part of the cultural acceptance between the culture and another culture, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the cultural acceptance tooltip of the culture window, next to the acceptance figures.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture the acceptance is about.

label: Acceptance changes text
summary: Text listing what changed the culture's acceptance of another culture.
details: Going by its name and its use in the cultural acceptance tooltip of the culture window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture the acceptance is about.

label: Acceptance change
summary: The difference in the cultural acceptance towards another culture, as a number that can be negative, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it with a plus or minus sign next to the acceptance, and the culture window hides that part when it is zero. What the difference is measured over is not shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture the acceptance is about.

label: Add tradition blockers
summary: Text naming the reasons the culture cannot add or replace a tradition right now, going by its name.
details: Vanilla puts it at the end of the tooltips of the establish-tradition and replace-tradition actions.

label: Average development
summary: The average development level of the culture's counties, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger. That it is an average over counties follows from its name.

label: Bonus fascination type
summary: The kind of fascination (the innovation focus) the culture gets a bonus for.
details: The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it. This rests on the name only.

label: Architecture name
summary: The name of the culture's architecture style.
details: Vanilla shows it as the 'Architecture' line in the culture aesthetics tooltip and in the hybridize window.

label: Clothing name
summary: The name of the culture's clothing style.
details: Vanilla shows it in the culture aesthetics tooltip and in the hybridize window.

label: Coat of arms style name
summary: The name of the culture's coat of arms style.
details: Vanilla shows it in the culture aesthetics tooltip and in the hybridize window.

label: Collective noun
summary: The word for the people of the culture as a group.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts like the fascination effect descriptions and in event texts. Going by the names, this version can show a tooltip and the NoTooltip version is plain text.

label: Collective noun (plain)
summary: The culture's word for its people as a group, as plain text without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it to build the group word of a new culture: when a culture splits off it writes "Neo-" in front of it, or a title's prefix and a hyphen. A plain text fits there because it becomes part of a new name.

label: Counties change
summary: The change in the number of counties of the culture, a whole number that can be negative.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign in the ledger. A ledger tooltip says the culture 'will gain' or 'will lose' counties, choosing by whether the number is above -1. The period it covers is not shown.

label: Counties gained
summary: A count of counties the culture gains, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger tooltip about the change in counties, which words it as 'will gain'. The time span is not shown by the input.

label: Counties lost
summary: A count of counties the culture loses, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger tooltip about the change in counties, which words it as 'will lose'. The time span is not shown by the input.

label: Creation date
summary: The date the culture was created.
details: The game documents no return type, but vanilla reads its year (GetYear) in the ledger, for example 'Est. year'. It is also compared with the current date.

label: Creation text
summary: Text about the culture's creation.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the culture window and as a ledger tooltip. What it says exactly is not shown, going by its name it is about the creation.

label: Dynasty arms frame
summary: The frame image for a dynasty's coat of arms of this culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the shared coat of arms GUI. The return type is not documented.

label: Dynasty arms mask
summary: The mask image for a dynasty's coat of arms of this culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms mask in the shared coat of arms GUI. The return type is not documented.

label: Dynasty arms offset
summary: The position offset of a dynasty's coat of arms of this culture, as a two-part vector.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms offset in the shared coat of arms GUI.

label: Dynasty arms scale
summary: The size scale of a dynasty's coat of arms of this culture, as a two-part vector.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms scale in the shared coat of arms GUI.

label: Culture era
summary: The era the culture is currently in.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads the era's name from it in the culture window tooltip.

label: Culture head
summary: The character who leads the culture (the cultural head).
details: Vanilla shows the head's name in tooltips and compares it with the player in the culture window. HasCultureHead exists, so there can be a culture without a head (inferred).

label: House arms frame
summary: The frame image for a house's coat of arms of this culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the shared coat of arms GUI. The return type is not documented.

label: House arms mask
summary: The mask image for a house's coat of arms of this culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms mask in the shared coat of arms GUI. The return type is not documented.

label: House arms offset
summary: The position offset of a house's coat of arms of this culture, as a two-part vector.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms offset in the shared coat of arms GUI.

label: House arms scale
summary: The size scale of a house's coat of arms of this culture, as a two-part vector.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms scale in the shared coat of arms GUI.

label: Divergence blockers
summary: Text naming the reasons the culture cannot diverge right now.
details: Going by its name and one tooltip of the diverge button, where it is called on the player's culture.

label: Ethos
summary: The culture's ethos.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads its name and icon from it, in the court type window and the ruler designer.

label: Current fascination
summary: The fascination (the innovation the culture currently focuses on).
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads its name from it and uses it as the data of a tooltip.

label: Fascination type
summary: The kind of fascination the culture has.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla only uses it in one situation window text, which compares the fascination types of two cultures (the player's and an innovation's) to pick a text.

label: Graphical unit type
summary: The culture's graphical unit type (the look of its soldiers).
details: The game documents no return type. The lines in the input use the same name after other types, such as a character's culture in the battle summary; this rests on those hints and the name.

label: Heritage
summary: The culture's heritage (the group of related cultures it belongs to).
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads its name from it and compares it between cultures.

label: Hybridization blockers
summary: Text naming the reasons the culture cannot form a hybrid with another culture.
details: Going by its name and one tooltip of the hybridize button, where it is called on the player's culture.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture to hybridize with.

label: Culture ID
summary: The culture's internal number (an unsigned whole number).
details: Vanilla passes it to the commands that open or toggle the culture window for this culture.

label: Innovation of type
summary: The culture's innovation of a given type.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla does not use it. This rests on the name only.

label: Language
summary: The culture's language pillar.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as the data of a block in the culture window and compares the languages of two cultures.

label: Martial custom
summary: The culture's martial custom (its martial pillar).
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as the data of a block in the culture window and compares it between two cultures.

label: Max traditions
summary: The most traditions the culture can have, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the second number in 'current/maximum' in the culture window.

label: Max traditions breakdown
summary: Text listing what makes up the culture's maximum number of traditions.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the culture window.

label: Culture name
summary: The culture's name.
details: Going by the names, this version can show a tooltip when hovered; GetNameNoTooltip returns plain text. Vanilla uses it in a great many texts, for example decision and travel event texts.

label: Culture name (plain)
summary: The culture's name without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as faction names and nicknames, where a tooltip would be unwanted.

label: Naming style name
summary: The name of the culture's naming style.
details: Vanilla shows it in the hybridize window. The input does not show how it differs from GetNamingListName, which that window shows too.

label: Naming list name
summary: The name of the culture's naming list ('Naming Practices').
details: Vanilla shows it as the 'Naming Practices' line in the culture aesthetics tooltip and in the hybridize window.

label: No head reason
summary: Text telling why the culture has no head.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the culture window. Going by its name it explains the missing head.

label: Number of characters
summary: How many characters have this culture, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and fades the row when it is zero.

label: Number of counties
summary: How many counties have this culture, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and hides the row when it is zero.

label: Discovered innovations
summary: How many innovations the culture has discovered, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the era tooltip of the culture window as '(n Innovations)'.

label: Number of rulers
summary: How many rulers have this culture, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and hides the row when it is zero.

label: Relation to player text
summary: Text describing how the culture relates to the player's culture.
details: Vanilla shows it in the culture window and in a tooltip. The exact wording of the relations is not shown by the input.

label: Culture prefix
summary: The culture's prefix word, used in front of a name.
details: Going by its name and the lines in the input, which use the same name after other types, as in 'Prefix-Hybrid culture'. Those lines may belong to other types, so this is a hint.

label: Culture prefix (plain)
summary: The culture's prefix, the short form of its name used to join it with another word, as plain text without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it to build the names of new cultures: a culture that splits off gets "Neo-" in front of the prefix, and a hybrid culture joins the other culture's prefix with a hyphen to this culture's name ("Prefix-Name").

label: Reformation
summary: The culture's current reformation (the change of pillars or traditions it is working on).
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as the data of a block in the culture window and reads the new pillar and a progress breakdown from it.

label: Relation to player
summary: How the culture relates to the player's culture.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla does not use it. This rests on the name only; GetPlayerRelationString is the text version.

label: Spread
summary: The culture's innovation spread, going by its name and a related text.
details: The game documents no return type. The only line in the input calls it on the culture of the culture window as the data of a block. A related function, GetSpreadingCulture, is used in the text 'innovation spread source'.

label: Spreading culture
summary: The culture an innovation is spreading from.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows its name in a text about the source of an innovation spread.

label: Culture template
summary: The culture's template, the data it was set up from.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as the data of a block in the ruler designer window. What exactly the template holds is not shown.

label: Culture template data
summary: The data of the culture's template.
details: The game documents no return type. The lines in the input use the same name after other types, for example a house's culture in the coat of arms GUI; those may belong to other types, so this rests on the name and those hints.

label: Total military strength
summary: The culture's total military strength, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger.

label: New tradition time breakdown
summary: Text listing what makes up the time to establish a new tradition.
details: Going by its name and the establishment-time tooltip, where it is called on the player's culture.

label: Pillar time breakdown
summary: Text listing what makes up the time to establish a new pillar.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip about the time to establish a pillar, below the total time.

label: Replace tradition time breakdown
summary: Text listing what makes up the time to replace a tradition.
details: Going by its name and the establishment-time tooltip, where it is called on the player's culture.

label: New tradition time
summary: Text giving the total time to establish a new tradition.
details: Vanilla shows it in the add-tradition window when the player is not replacing a tradition.

label: Pillar time
summary: Text giving the total time to establish a new pillar.
details: Vanilla shows it in the replace-pillar window and in the establishment-time tooltip.

label: Replace tradition time
summary: Text giving the total time to replace a tradition.
details: Vanilla shows it in the add-tradition window when the player is replacing a tradition.

label: Traditions
summary: The list of the culture's traditions.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as the list a GUI block loops over and counts its size in the culture window.

label: Unit style name
summary: The name of the culture's unit style (the look of its soldiers).
details: Vanilla shows it in the culture aesthetics tooltip and in the hybridize window.

label: Yearly acceptance text
summary: Text explaining the yearly change in the culture's acceptance of another culture.
details: Going by its name and its use in the cultural acceptance tooltip of the culture window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The other culture the acceptance is about.

label: Has available innovation
summary: Whether the culture has an innovation available, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture tooltip together with checks that the culture is the player's (and, once, that the player is its head), to show or hide elements.

label: Has culture head
summary: Whether the culture has a head.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window to show the head's block or the no-head block.

label: Has fascination
summary: Whether the culture currently has a fascination.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the culture window and its tooltip.

label: Has spread
summary: Whether the culture has an innovation spread.
details: Going by its name and the culture window lines, which call it on the window's culture to show or hide blocks. Those lines may belong to other types, so this is a hint.

label: Is child of
summary: Whether the culture grew out of the given culture.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window to show relations between the viewed culture and the player's culture, both ways round.

label: Is player culture
summary: Whether the culture is the player's culture.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla does not use it. This rests on the name only.

label: Is player culture head
summary: Whether the player is the head of this culture.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it in the culture tooltip, together with a check that the culture is the player's, to show or hide elements.

label: Is player heritage
summary: Whether the culture has the same heritage as the player's culture.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla does not use it. This rests on the name only.

label: Is reforming
summary: Whether the culture is in the middle of a reformation.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch a tooltip text of the reform action, to show a part of the add-tradition window, and to disable an element of the culture window while it is true.

label: Culture is valid
summary: Whether the culture exists (is not empty).
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the HUD, the intrigue window and the ledger only when there is a culture. That it means 'exists' rests on this use and the name.

label: Culture as scope
summary: Turns the culture into a script scope object that other functions can work with.
details: Vanilla uses it to hand the culture to the watch window command. The return type is a scope.

label: Open add tradition
summary: Opens the window for adding a tradition to the culture.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button in the culture window is clicked.

label: Open divergence
summary: Opens the window for diverging the culture.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button in the culture window is clicked.

label: Open hybridization
summary: Opens the window for forming a hybrid culture.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button in the culture window is clicked.

label: Open replace ethos
summary: Opens the window for replacing the culture's ethos.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button in the culture window is clicked.

label: Open replace language
summary: Opens the window for replacing the culture's language, going by its name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla's GUI files do not use it.

label: Open replace martial
summary: Opens the window for replacing the culture's martial custom.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button in the culture window is clicked.

label: Open replace tradition
summary: Opens the window for replacing one of the culture's traditions.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a tradition is clicked in the culture window.

label: Culture
summary: The culture itself, as an object to pass on to other functions.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example into the pillar effect description. The name Self exists on many types.

label: Suggest ancestor name
summary: Whether the culture's naming custom suggests naming a child after an ancestor.
details: Vanilla uses it in the name-child event widget to show the ancestor name suggestion.

label: Suggest family name
summary: Whether the culture's naming custom suggests a family name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the name-child event widget to show the family name suggestion.

label: Aesthetics (access)
summary: The culture aesthetics entry itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Going by its name only; the example lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Aesthetics description
summary: The description text of a culture aesthetics entry.
details: Vanilla shows it under the name in the aesthetics tooltip of the divergence window.

label: Aesthetics name
summary: The name of a culture aesthetics entry.
details: Vanilla shows it in the aesthetics tooltip of the divergence window.

label: Aesthetics
summary: The culture aesthetics entry itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla passes it to the divergence window to check or set the chosen aesthetic.

label: Era (access)
summary: The culture era itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Going by its name only; the example lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Era can gain progress
summary: Whether the culture can gain progress towards this era.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it in the culture window and tooltip to show progress or the reason it is not possible.

label: Can progress to next era
summary: Whether the culture can move on to the next era.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Why no era progress
summary: Text telling why the culture cannot gain progress towards the era.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows it in the culture window and its tooltip.

label: Era's culture
summary: The culture this era belongs to.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads the culture's collective noun from it in the era tile texts.

label: Era progress estimate
summary: Text giving an estimate of the progress towards the era.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows it in the culture window, only when it is not empty.

label: Era name
summary: The name of the culture era, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window's innovation texts, such as "Must first reach the ... era" and how many innovations of an era are needed before the next one.

label: Era name (plain)
summary: The name of the culture era without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in era tile texts of the culture window.

label: Active innovations in era
summary: How many of the era's innovations are active, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first number of 'active/total' and as a progress bar value in the ledger.

label: Innovations in era
summary: How many innovations the era has in total, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the second number of 'active/total' and as the maximum of a progress bar in the ledger.

label: Era progress
summary: The culture's progress towards the era, as a number.
details: Vanilla converts it to a plain number and uses it as the value of a progress bar in the culture window.

label: Era progress breakdown
summary: Text listing the progress towards the era and what adds to it.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the culture window and as text in the culture tooltip.

label: Era type
summary: The type of the era (for example which era it is).
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads the era's illustration from it and uses it as the data of a tooltip block.

label: Era is active
summary: Whether the era is active for the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window to show or hide parts of an era tile.

label: Era
summary: The culture era itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla does not use it with this type; the lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Era type (access)
summary: The culture era type itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Going by its name only; the example lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Era type description
summary: The description text of the era type.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in a shared tooltip.

label: Era effects text
summary: Text describing the effects of the era type for a culture and a character.
details: Vanilla calls it once, with the era's culture and the player, as the text of a tooltip. The meaning of the two arguments is read from that one use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are for (in vanilla: the era's culture).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character the effects are described for (in vanilla: the player).

label: Era type frame
summary: The frame number of the era type's icon, going by its name.
details: The game documents no return type. The lines in the input use the same name after other types; this is a hint at best.

label: Era type picture
summary: The illustration of the era type.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla reads it through CultureEra.GetType in the culture window as a texture. The lines listed for this type in the input belong to other types.

label: Era type name
summary: The name of the era type.
details: The lines in the input that use the same name belong to other types, so this rests on the name and the type.

label: Era type year
summary: A year of the era type, as a whole number; what the year marks is not shown.
details: The lines in the input that use the same name belong to dates, not to this type, so only the name and the return type are known.

label: Era type has effects
summary: Whether the era type has effects for a culture and a character.
details: Vanilla calls it once, with the era's culture and the player, to show or hide an element of a tooltip. The meaning of the two arguments is read from that one use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are for (in vanilla: the era's culture).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character the effects are checked for (in vanilla: the player).

label: Era type has frame
summary: Whether the era type has an icon frame, going by its name.
details: The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Era type has picture
summary: Whether the era type has an illustration, going by its name.
details: The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Invalid for player government
summary: Whether the era type does not fit the player's government.
details: Going by its name and the culture window lines, which call it on an era's type to show or hide a notice. Those lines may belong to other types, so this is a hint.

label: Era type
summary: The culture era type itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla does not use it with this type; the lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Innovation (access)
summary: The culture innovation itself, as an object to pass on.
details: The game documents no return type. Going by its name only; the example lines in the input belong to other types.

label: Can be fascination
summary: Whether the innovation can be chosen as the culture's fascination.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it in the culture window to enable or show or hide innovation tiles.

label: Innovation can gain progress
summary: Whether the innovation can gain progress.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window and the silk road window to show or hide parts of an innovation tile, often together with a check that it is not active.

label: Player can set as fascination
summary: Whether the player can set the innovation as the culture's fascination.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it to show an element only when the innovation is not already the fascination.

label: Bonus progress text
summary: Text describing the bonus progress of the innovation.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the culture window.

label: Why no innovation progress
summary: Text telling why the innovation cannot gain progress.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in a shared tooltip.

label: Innovation's culture
summary: The culture the innovation belongs to.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla checks it for the player's culture head and for the culture's fascination type.

label: Innovation's era
summary: The era the innovation belongs to.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows its name with the word 'era' and compares it with the selected era in the culture window.

label: Innovation description
summary: The description text of the innovation.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in a shared tooltip.

label: Innovation icon
summary: The icon image of the innovation.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla uses it as a texture in the culture window.

label: Innovation state
summary: Text for the state the innovation is in.
details: The game documents no return type. Vanilla shows it as text in the culture window. Which states exist is not shown by the input.

label: Innovation name
summary: The name of the innovation.
details: This version can show a tooltip. Vanilla shows it in the culture window and the silk road window.

label: Innovation name (plain)
summary: The name of the innovation without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as the silk road travel text.

label: Innovation progress
summary: The innovation's progress, as a number out of 100.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'Progress: n/100' and converts it to a plain number for a progress bar.

label: Innovation progress chance
summary: The monthly chance that the innovation gains progress, shown as a percentage.
